Before your first inquiry

Getting started

You don’t need to arrive with a finished research plan. Start with a question that interests you, then check whether the lab offers a suitable undergraduate role.

01

Build a small, focused list.

Compare the research topic, required coursework, weekly hours and semester commitment. Save several groups you could explain a clear interest in. For a faculty or center lead, undergraduate intake still needs to be established.

02

Read the lab’s instructions.

Open “Full details” for the evidence behind each listing. Check the intended term, contact, prerequisites and any application form. When two sources disagree, confirm the point with the lab. Use the application route it requests.

DIS enrollment, credit, supervision and registration requirements vary by department. Ask your academic advisor before assuming a placement will earn credit.

03

Send a specific introduction.

Read a recent lab paper or project description. Explain the topic that interests you, one relevant experience, and the hours and term you can commit. Edit every bracketed placeholder in the CELLS template, attach your résumé, and proofread the recipient and attachment.

04

Confirm the arrangement.

Before accepting, ask what your work will involve, how you will be trained, who supervises you, and whether the role is paid, volunteer or for credit. Confirm weekly hours, duration, location and required training. An inquiry, public listing or application does not guarantee an offer.

If a lab does not reply, one brief follow-up after about a week is a reasonable courtesy; follow any instructions that set a different timeline or ask for no further emails.

05

Use the campus routes.

UROP is a structured program with its own application and matching process. Honors in the Major, department research courses and other CRE opportunities have separate eligibility and deadlines.

CELLS member resources

Outreach & résumé templates

Edit the CELLS email templates below, then copy or download your message. Edits are not saved, so copy your text before you leave the page.

Faster: open any lab in the directory and tap Draft an email. The lab’s details and yours are filled in, and the draft opens in your mail app.

Make the message your own
  • Replace every bracketed placeholder with accurate details.
  • Use a specific paper, project or finding from the professor’s work.
  • State the term and weekly hours you can realistically commit.
  • Attach your résumé and check the lab’s requested application method.

Copy the wording below into your email app. Editing, copying and downloading need a full browser.

First inquiry

Subject: Undergraduate Research Inquiry — [Research Topic] — [Term]

Dear Professor [Last Name],

My name is [Your Name], and I am a [year] majoring in [major] at [university]. I am reaching out to express my interest in contributing to your research group during [term].

I came across your [paper or project] on [specific topic] and was particularly interested in [specific finding, method, or research question]. [One sentence explaining why this aspect interests you or how it connects to something you have studied or explored.]

Through [relevant coursework, project, or experience], I have [specific example of what you learned or accomplished], developing a foundation in [relevant skill or subject]. I would welcome the opportunity to apply this background to your research while learning additional methods. I can commit [number] hours per week during [term].

Would you be open to a brief conversation about possible undergraduate research opportunities, either with you or a member of your group? I have attached my resume for your reference.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best regards,

[Your Full Name]
[Major] | [University]
[University Email]
Follow-up

Subject: Re: Undergraduate Research Inquiry — [Research Topic] — [Term]

Dear Professor [Last Name],

I wanted to briefly follow up on my previous email regarding undergraduate research opportunities in your group for [term].

I remain very interested in your work on [research topic] and would appreciate the opportunity to discuss whether there might be a way to get involved.

Thank you again for your time and consideration.

Best regards,

[Your Full Name]

About

This directory was designed and built by Macin Bennetts, Scholarship & Internship Chair of FSU CELLS, for CELLS members. It draws on public FSU lab pages, department directories and the UROP project database, and was last updated October 26, 2026. Listings change, so check each lab’s own page before you apply.

CELLS placements

Found a mistake?

Send the lab name, what changed and a link to the source to a CELLS board member, and we’ll fix it.

How we checked every listing
429Research records, including historical entries
160Projects in the current public UROP database
554Source pages rechecked on October 26

What this directory establishes

The 429 records comprise 122 labs or research groups, 26 programs and routes, 87 faculty or center leads, and 194 UROP records. Of the UROP records, 160 are publicly listed in the current database. The other 34 are kept for reference: 21 historical records from the original guide and 13 projects removed from the database between October 13 and October 26. Closed and expired records are hidden in the directory until you include them.

This is not a census of every unpublished lab or every available seat. An institutional research profile establishes an interest lead; it does not establish undergraduate eligibility or capacity. Dated invitations, undated application routes and inquiry contacts are labeled separately. Requested UROP staffing totals are not counts of remaining seats.

The latest pass checked 357 linked sources and 163 UROP detail pages: 509 of the 520 checks returned HTTP 200. Eleven retrievals failed or were blocked. A successful retrieval alone does not establish that a page is complete or current. Limited retrievals are marked in record details, and failures are not treated as evidence that a lab has closed. An October 13 recheck reopened every UROP project page and most lab and faculty pages, and its corrections are applied.

On October 26, every one of the 554 linked source pages was fetched again: 541 loaded normally and 13 were blocked or failed for technical reasons, which are not treated as closures. The recheck also compared the full UROP database and the Psychology DIS list. Changes: 13 UROP projects left the public database, one UROP project title changed, the Plant Lab Spring 2027 window closed (next window about March 1–15, 2027) and the ACR Lab Spring 2027 deadline passed. No new DIS listings or UROP projects appeared.

How conflicts were handled

Lab-specific instructions and dated notices take priority over older or undated departmental language. Where public sources disagree, the detail view shows the conflict and asks members to confirm it. Application forms are kept distinct from study-participant recruitment. Faculty affiliations are cross-checked where possible; unconfirmed undergraduate intake is labeled.

Keep the guide useful

Before applying, open the source and confirm dates, instructions and capacity. If you find an error, send the lab name, changed fact and official source link to a CELLS executive board member. The board should review dated windows before each semester and check departmental rosters when updating the guide.

The seal was supplied by CELLS. The design uses FSU’s published garnet and gold palette, Open Sans, and EB Garamond as an open serif companion. This student resource is not an official university vacancy database.
